name: Central Nervous System Embryonal Tumor
aliases: Embryonal Tumor of the Central Nervous System

criteria.description: Histopathological identification of undifferentiated or poorly differentiated neuroepithelial cells
Presence of characteristic molecular alterations such as MYC amplification or specific gene fusions
MRI showing a well-demarcated, often contrast-enhancing mass in the CNS

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation with supportive molecular genetic findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of histology and molecular genetics per WHO CNS tumor classification.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Signs of increased intracranial pressure (e.g., papilledema, headache)

common.symptomName: Nausea and vomiting related to intracranial hypertension
searchTerms: nausea caused by increased head pressure
cranial nerve palsies causing facial or eye problems

rare.symptomName: Endocrine dysfunction due to hypothalamic involvement
searchTerms: hormone problems from brain area damage
endocrine issues due to hypothalamus involvement
hormonal imbalance caused by brain tumor

laboratory: CSF cytology may show malignant cells
Elevated CSF protein in some cases
imaging: MRI with contrast showing well-demarcated mass with heterogeneous enhancement
Possible evidence of hydrocephalus on imaging
genetic: Alterations in TP53, CTNNB1, or other oncogenes/tumor suppressor genes
Specific gene fusions depending on tumor subtype
other: Histopathology showing small round blue cells with high mitotic activity
Immunohistochemistry positive for neuronal markers (e.g., synaptophysin)

redFlags: New onset seizures in a child
references: Louis DN, et al. WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System, 5th Edition. IARC, 2021.
Orphanet: Central nervous system embryonal tumor - ORPHA:251870
Packer RJ, et al. Pediatric CNS Tumors: Diagnosis and Treatment. Neurology Clinics, 2020.
